description: Space Buds is a group of Computer Science university students who ended up meeting for the first time in their local competition this space apps. Space Buds seeks to have their application be able to leave an impact and lasting impression.
summary: The project we developed is an analysis took that addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator Challenge. The project allows for Luna to be viewed in place at in orbit at a selected date and time. Luna's LOLA elevation map, LOLA PSR map, LRO Diviner temperature map. The application can calculate maps of expected connectivity calculated based off the LOLA elevation terrain mapping and either input mounting height and mounting angle, or a default value of mounted at 1m at 0 degrees for receivers. The application also can calculate maps and expected power generation across the moons surface, as well as power generated over time at the selected location, by the LOLA elevation graph for terrain, input solar panel efficiency rate, mounting angle, and mounting height, or the default values of 30% at 1m, and 0 degrees. Upon clicking a location the application shows you 2 vectors if both the sun and earth are visible, where the blue one is the direction to the visible earth, and yellow is the direction to the visible sun. If they aren't visible these vectors wont show. The angle of the vectors is shown in specific in the further information below the 3D map view.
details:
Our solution uses data from the LRO Diviner temperature datasets, LOLA elevation data, PSR maps, and SPICE kernels to serve as both a comparison tool and a 3D mapping tool for identifying landing sites on Luna's surface. Our solution aims to streamline landing site selection and comparison by consolidating all information in one place for the mission planner to analyze and compare. Our solution is made of multiple languages, including Python (for SPICEpy), JavaScript, CSS, and HTML. Our project is unique in that it allows it to be viewed in a 3-dimensional space with all the information easily accessible. Our team considered power generation, communication, the moon at various times, solar panel mounting height and angle, power efficiency, communication antenna mounting height and angle, elevation of the terrain, and PSR locations.

In short, Moon Walk helps mission planners, educators, and the public compare landing sites and dates quickly, visualizing Sun and Earth positions relative to the horizon to assess power generation potential and direct-to-Earth communication windows.
